Hi Amy —

Below are focused answers and evidence references for the SIG access control items you listed. I’ve kept any sensitive identifiers masked; if you need raw logs we can exchange via a secure share.

SSO / SAML
- Flows supported: SP-initiated and IdP-initiated both supported.
- IdP metadata: https://accounts.redwood.com/saml/metadata.xml (this is our public SP metadata).
- Assertions: we include Subject, NameID (transient or persistent as configured), and group membership as an attribute (Groups).
- Enforcement: SAML assertions are validated with our SP certificate; assertion expiry enforced (short lifetime).

SCIM provisioning
- Base URL (SCIM v2): https://provisioning.redwood.com/scim/v2/
- Auth: OAuth2 Bearer token with client credentials grant; tokens are short-lived and rotated every 90 days by default.
- Scoping: SCIM only syncs a subset of user attributes (userName, externalId, emails, active, groups). We explicitly map SCIM groups to Redwood roles.
- Evidence: attached role_mapping_example.csv and a redacted provisioning log bundle scim-provisioning-logs-20261119.zip showing a successful PATCH add of a user to the "Operators" group.

RBAC & least privilege
- Principle: least privilege by default. Roles are narrow and composable. Examples in authorization_matrix_v1.csv (attached):
  - Viewer: read-only access to tenant resources and logs
  - Operator: create/scale inference deployments, not permitted to change billing or organization-level settings
  - Admin: full tenant config, user management
  - Billing: view and manage invoices only
  - Security-Admin: can view audit logs and manage SSO configs but cannot change billing
- Role membership sources: groups from SCIM (primary), optional manual assignment by Admin.
- Enforcement: RBAC checks are enforced at the API gateway layer and in the runtime control plane (deny by default for unknown principals).

MFA & service accounts
- MFA: Required for all interactive users. We integrate with IdP-level MFA (Okta, Azure AD) and require at least two factors for admin-level roles.
- Service accounts: no interactive password-based accounts; service principals use OAuth2 client credentials with scoped certificates and short-lived tokens. Keys are rotated and each service principal has constrained permissions. We log every token issuance and rotation event.

Evidence and next steps
- Attached: role_mapping_example.csv, scim-provisioning-logs-20261119.zip.
- We will provide a redacted SAML assertion sample and a signed declarative statement for SIG Q2.3 by Monday COB.
- Link to more detail: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bRoleMatrixExample (contains role docs and the playbook).

If you want, Hannah can run a 20-minute walkthrough of the role matrix and provisioning flow early next week.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Amy —

Quick clarification on a few operational points you asked about:

- Group-to-role sync cadence: SCIM group syncs happen near-real time; group membership changes propagate within ~30s in typical loads.
- Manual exceptions: when a manual role grant is required (rare), we record a ticket and require a justification and time-bound expiry.
- Audit sampling: for your request we pulled an anonymized audit entry showing a successful SCIM PATCH (user add to group) and a corresponding RBAC evaluation log that resulted in the Operator role being applied. That entry is inside scim-provisioning-logs-20261119.zip.

Attached also: service_accounts_inventory.csv — a CSV of active non-human principals and their assigned roles (identifiers obfuscated). If you need unaudited raw IDs for your SOC reviewer, we can coordinate an NDA-guarded transfer.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
